title: Rendering, preview and analysis
objective: Give the compiled entry stage-boundary methods before Corrections adds a boundary, and measure and bound the GPU resources outside the provisional photo-texture ceiling before any total-memory guarantee.
context_summary: Rendering has one entry point (luxforge_core::render) with an injected RenderContext, one latest-job worker, one tile function and one point pipeline generic over the byte and linear pixel domains, so a sample equals the rendered byte by construction; one table test proves it over every stack shape and both domains. Limits have one home, frames are opaque, render.rs is split by concept and the byte-identical speedups are recorded in docs/specs/performance.md. The 1088 MiB temporary photo-texture overlap ceiling is provisionally accepted for those slots only (2026-09-27); crop GPU textures, overlays and backend staging remain outside it and are not measured or bounded, so no total-memory guarantee is made. The stage-boundary task is roadmap groundwork, blocked until Corrections starts. Decisions and constraints: docs/decisions.md and docs/design/post-consolidation.md.

tasks.description: Give the compiled Entry a small set of methods for what its match arms ask today, so a new stage-boundary kind becomes one implementation instead of a new arm in about 30 places.
extra_context: Wave 6, roadmap groundwork. Blocked: starts with the Corrections repair stage, the third kind of stage boundary; a trait is premature with only two kinds in the code today.

Entry (render.rs) is matched in about 30 places across six files: render.rs, render/pipeline.rs, render/window.rs, render/linear.rs, render/entry.rs and modules/registry/compile.rs (file names as today; the render.rs split moves some). The Corrections proposal's repair stage would add a case to each: the point walk (Evaluation::entry_pixel), the byte driver (rasterize), Evaluation::new and SpatialEntry::of, window planning, locate, the linear rows (LinearRows) and compilation. SpatialEntry (render/pipeline.rs) already gathers the spatial arm's own questions in one type, which is the shape these methods generalise.

A GPU colour stage would need a per-unit typed description; PointwiseColor (modules/processing.rs) exposes only apply_row, is_finite and describe, with no way to extract a unit's kind and coefficients. spatial::prefix_hash (render/spatial.rs) already gives an out-of-process AI patch the input-prefix hash its design needs, so that part does not wait on this.

Proposal, once the Corrections repair stage starts: give Entry methods for what the match arms currently ask by hand, an input-stage query, mapping a point back through the entry, the rectangle it reads, materialising it, and evaluating one point through it, so a new stage-boundary kind implements those methods once instead of adding an arm at each of the roughly 30 sites.

Renders and samples stay byte-identical on both pixel domains: this is a refactor of dispatch, not of arithmetic, provable with the existing suites.

The new stage-boundary kind's own tests pass through the same methods, not a new arm set.

tasks.description: Measure and bound GPU resources excluded from the provisional 1088 MiB photo-texture ceiling before making a total-memory guarantee.
extra_context: Not in a programme wave, by the owner's decision of 2026-09-28 (docs/decisions.md, "Plan refresh"): a standalone follow-up that the provisional acceptance of the photo-texture ceiling (2026-09-27) requires before any total-memory claim, run beside the whole-editor RAW measurement, which already needs native M4 GPU allocations and holds the largest photos. It depends on no other rendering task.

The owner provisionally accepted the 1088 MiB temporary-overlap ceiling on 2026-09-27 for the photo surface slots alone: one current and one retiring full-photo allocation up to 512 MiB each, and two region sets up to 32 MiB each. This is an engineering ceiling, not a total editor or GPU budget. The ceiling is one photo-texture budget shared by every photo surface (decided 2026-09-28), so a second surface draws from it rather than doubling it.

Crop GPU textures and tiles, overlays and backend-owned upload staging are outside that accounting. Since the crop's proxy stage landed, a crop draft's input-stage texture is reserved at exactly its frame's size: the display-size proxy at Fit (6.7 MiB on the generated 60 MP JPEG and 7.5 MiB on the X100VI, about 11 MiB of GPU allocation per open draft; docs/specs/performance.md, 'A crop draft's input stage at Fit'), and a full-size exact stage only at a percentage zoom that needs one, tiled past the 8192 px texture limit and capped only by the core's 512 MiB frame limit (229 MiB for a 60 MP stage). The clipping and mask overlays have textures of their own, and backend staging is still unmeasured. editor-latency's crop-start mode reads memory at Fit only; the exact stage at a percentage zoom needs a measured path. Use representative 24 MP and 60 MP workflows and native M4 GPU evidence, including temporary overlap and retirement, before proposing a total bound.

acceptance_criteria: Native M4 evidence accounts separately for photo slots, crop GPU textures and tiles, overlays, and backend upload staging on representative 24 MP and 60 MP workloads, including temporary overlap and resource retirement.

Each excluded allocation path has an enforced byte cap or a derived peak-byte bound from bounded allocation sizes and maximum simultaneous overlap, including retirement; resource-limit behavior is explicit where a cap refuses work.
The measured scope and any resulting total editor/GPU bound are documented without treating the 1088 MiB photo ceiling as a process-wide guarantee; Windows/Linux remain separately qualified.

steps: Inventory crop, overlay and backend GPU allocation and retirement paths; capture native GPU allocations during representative Fit and 100% crop, edit and pan transitions at 24 MP and 60 MP, extending editor-latency's crop-start mode to a percentage zoom where the exact stage needs it.
Add the smallest enforceable accounting or limits for omitted resources and verify overlap, retirement and refusal behavior in focused surface tests.
Repeat native measurement on the bounded implementation, correlate GPU and process counters with application slot logs, and update the design, performance evidence and feature status.
